findings_qualitative.value: Disk of HD163296 is weakly detected as a broken ring with a surface brightness drop inward of 0.6''; no polarized emission from HD141569A and HD150193A

evidence.quote: The disk is resolved as a broken ring structure with a significant surface brightness drop inward of $0.6\ensuremath{''}$.

claims.hypothesis: The inner light drop in HD163296 is caused by self-shadowing versus alternatives such as CO ice
claims.experiment: Compare PDI contrast with DCO+ ALMA map and geometric arguments
claims.result: Contrast rises by >~6 over the same interval where DCO+ rises, but ALMA resolution is low
claims.finding: Self-shadowing is favored; CO freeze-out is only tantalizing

evidence.quote: Even though we have a propensity for the self-shadowing scenario, we cannot firmly establish the origin of the polarized-light deficit

limitations_admitted.value: Low ALMA angular resolution prevents strong conclusions from spatial coincidence

evidence.quote: prevents us from drawing strong conclusions from the possible spatial coincidence of the two datasets
